work.title: Redwood front-door ingestion and UX acceptance path

intent.productGoal: Enable a professional user to create a new engagement and bring unfamiliar evidence through the product UI into a governed canonical engagement.
intent.capability: New engagement, ZIP/individual source intake, source inventory/recognition/preview, mapping, G1 sufficiency, immutable run creation, and Reconcile handoff.
architecturalIntent: Build on the existing Redwood Workbench rather than a parallel application.
Drive evidence enters only through user-facing intake; hidden truth is excluded from normal ingestion.
invariants: Original source bytes and hashes remain preserved.
No silent source coercion or back-door test injection.
Visible active engagement values derive from uploaded evidence.

observedBehaviour: Browser intake ed7ec67f-4ccf-402c-96c2-625b8813e4c9 promoted through visible Run Redwood into run a80d93e0-7f05-425f-9715-e480e481066e.
Core Challenge A source controls matched after the run was frozen: 480 claims, $153,520.10 billed, $53,489.83 allowed, $37,274.33 cash, $16,215.50 A/R, and $5,544.18 120+ A/R.
Bank and ERA relationship controls were not materialized in the current canonical state.

evidence.result: Browser journey, frozen IDs, post-run truth comparison and UX assessment recorded.

evidence.reference: pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test
evidence.result: Build/typecheck passed and 20 core tests passed.

divergences.expected: Challenge A includes bank and ERA relationship truth assertions.
divergences.observed: Bank Deposits is inventoried as supporting evidence but is not materialized into current canonical/reconciliation relationships; Bank_Total and ERA_to_Bank_Difference could not be compared.

divergences.expected: Mapping review minimises cognitive load through grouped action-required workflow.
divergences.observed: Full inventory is accessible but still a lengthy table, with no complete Action Required grouping.
